**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Canonicalize the embedded request in receipt identity**

When two receipts contain the same parsed work request but serialize `receipt.original` with different whitespace or property order, an importer can recompute `requestSha256` and the receiver size totals so both receipts pass validation. Because `receiptId` hashes the receipt including that raw request string, the receipts receive different semantic IDs and bypass the duplicate checks in the evidence history and docket, allowing the same inspection to be charged twice. Build the semantic identity from the canonical parsed request and normalized receipt fields, while retaining `receiptDigest` for exact-byte identity.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Abort RPC work when the observation deadline expires**

When a fetch-backed `rpc` call does not settle before the per-call or total deadline, this `Promise.race` returns an inconclusive observation but only clears the timer; it never aborts the underlying request because the RPC receives only the caller's signal. The network operation can therefore continue consuming resources after the supposedly bounded inspection has returned. Use an internal abort controller linked to the caller signal and abort it on timeout or total-deadline expiry.
